newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Douwe Egberts raises Dutch retail coffee price.
newsitem.headline: Douwe Egberts raises Dutch retail coffee price.

text.p: Douwe Egberts, the leading Dutch coffee roaster, said on Wednesday it would be raising the retail price of coffee in the Netherlands with immediate effect in response to the sharp rise in world prices.

A spokesman for the company, owned by the giant Sara Lee Corporation of the United States, told Reuters the price of a 250-gramme pack of coffee would be raised by 20 cents, making it retail at an average of four guilders.
"It is Douwe Egberts' policy to change the retail price in response to the higher structural price of green coffee on the world market," spokesman Joost den Haan said.
Douwe Egberts holds some 70 percent of the Dutch market.

The world price of arabica coffee, quoted in New York, has doubled since late 1996 in a rally reignited last week on fears over tight Latin American supply and the onset of the Brazilian frost season. London-traded robusta futures are also strong, having jumped by around one-third since the start of the year.
